latin: Ioachin in prophetiis suis alia uia non processit quam per numeros formales.
translation: Joachim, in his prophecies, proceeded by no way other than through formal numbers.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch16, from Latin at farmer1998:23728
doctrine: The conclusion assigns Joachim of Fiore's prophetic method entirely to formal number, the same category of number that 7>9 credits with a route to natural prophecy (farmer1998:23724, farmer1998:23728). Farmer identifies 'Ioachin' as Joachim of Fiore and cross-refers to his own earlier discussion of the abbot (farmer1998:23792).
historiography: John Dee cites this conclusion in his Mathematicall Praeface as authority for his own numerology, in a passage naming 'the noble Earle of Mirandula' as witness that Joachim proceeded by formal numbers alone (quoted in mandosio2012:229). Mandosio treats the passage as a direct early modern use of the conclusion (mandosio2012:229).

quotations.text: Part of this profound and divine Science, had Joachim the Prophesier atteyned unto: by Numbers Formall, Naturall, and Rationall, forseyng, concludyng, and forshewyng great particular events, long before their comming ... And the noble Earle of Mirandula, (besides that,) a sufficient witnesse: that Joachim, in his prophesies, proceded by no other way, then by Numbers Formall.
quotations.note: John Dee's words, quoted within Mandosio's article; cited here at Mandosio's locator.
